p0.title: Night decree: shame is canceled
p0.intro: The Council has scrapped the requirement to apologize for who you are. Moral panic doesn’t get a veto.
p0.b0: We, the self-appointed Council of Zakon Czarnego Kału, after consulting one skeleton and the last brain cell with any common sense left, declare an end to doing penance for other people’s prejudices.
p0.b1: § 1. Gay pride isn’t an application for approval. A guy can love a guy without a stamp from the Committee on Other People’s Bedrooms.
p0.b2: § 2. Anyone who sees two men holding hands and starts yelling about the collapse of civilization should check whether theirs was built out of soggy cardboard.
p0.b3: § 3. The Order expects loyalty to its principles: consent, freedom and mutual respect. No title gets you out of thinking for yourself.
p0.b4: The decree bears the Black Seal. Appeals may be addressed to the Grand Chancellor of None of Your Business.
p1.title: Practical necromancy: this dead dogma isn’t getting up
p1.intro: Bring a skeleton back to life? Easy. Make sense of dead prejudices? That’s beyond even the Order’s powers.
p1.b0: In our made-up crypt, the necromancer revives memes, jokes and the courage to be yourself. Bringing back the idea that someone else’s sexuality is up for public judgment? There’s no budget for that.
p1.b1: A skeleton has one advantage over a hypocrite: at least it doesn’t pretend to have a moral backbone. The bar’s low, but the Council counts every win.
p1.b2: Being gay isn’t a curse. Thinking your own fear gives you the right to run someone else’s love life is. We don’t cast that spell.
p1.b3: The rule of Zakon Czarnego Kału is simple: bring humor back to life, bury contempt and respect consent. If a ritual means taking someone’s dignity away, throw out the ritual.
p2.title: Decree No. 001: on getting serious
p2.intro: The Council has decided that, from now on, trivial matters get the full ceremonial treatment.
p2.b0: From the day this decree is announced, everything the Order does must look serious. What we actually do is up to us. A sensible amount of nonsense is encouraged.
p2.b1: § 1. Any get-together can count as a Council meeting if at least one person says, “Right, listen up.”
p2.b2: § 2. The first person to ask if anyone’s taking notes gets the job. Even without notes, it can still count as a good get-together.
p2.b3: § 3. Hand out titles in moderation. Approved posts include Grand Keeper of the Charger and Commissioner for Things That Were Only Supposed to Take a Minute.
p2.b4: The decree takes effect as soon as you’ve read it. You can appeal, but you’ll need a better joke.
p3.title: First came the sketch. And the arrow.
p3.intro: Every legend needs a beginning. Ours fit into a single WhatsApp photo.
p3.b0: There was no competition, committee or forty-slide strategy presentation. There was a friend’s hand-drawn sketch: a symbol, an arrow, a few wisps and three letters. ZCK.
p3.b1: That sketch became our emblem. We kept the key bits: the stylized shape, the diagonal arrow and the four wisps. Then we gave it a much grander treatment than the subject ever called for.
p3.b2: That’s how the Order works: take a shared joke, build a story around it and see where imagination takes it.
p3.b3: This post opens the chronicle. What happens next is up to life and the group chat.
p4.title: A short guide to not taking yourself too seriously
p4.intro: Can something with no goal still have a direction? Sure. There’s an arrow on the crest.
p4.b0: Plenty of things in life need to be taken seriously. That’s why it’s good to have somewhere to drop the official tone for a minute. Then put it straight back on, just for the joke.
p4.b1: A little self-awareness helps you remember that being Grand Chancellor of Unimportant Affairs doesn’t make you more important than the person who just came to hang out.
p4.b2: Our rule’s simple: a good joke leaves room for everyone at the table. If someone’s not in the mood to laugh, there’s no need to launch an investigation.
p4.b3: And what’s the point of all this? Having something to look back on. A perfectly serious reason.
